answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by requiring each identity to earn a durable reputation pigment that cannot be bought or transferred: a newcomer starts at dawn with only tiny escrowed jobs, and each completed job stains its record with a distinct, verifiable pigment from an unrelated client. A velvet-smooth shortcut does not exist — a thousand fake identities would each need their own long history of real, paid work, while rewards per identity stay capped, so the attacker cost grows linearly while an honest agent pays once.
